'Ikrimah said: the woe is not for the one who withholds these things; rather the woe is for the one who gathers them, so he shows off in his prayer, forgets it, and withholds these. Al-Zajjaj said: al-Ma'un in the Jahiliyyah was everything that had benefit in it, like the axe, the pot, the bucket, the tinderbox, and the like, and also in Islam.

The second: that it is zakah. This was said by 'Ali, Ibn Ya'mar, al-Hasan, 'Ikrimah, and Qatadah.

The third: that it is obedience. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas in one report.

The fourth: wealth. This was said by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Zuhri.

The fifth: good (al-ma'ruf). This was said by Muhammad ibn Ka'b.

The sixth: water. Al-Farra' mentioned it from some Arabs, saying: and he recited to me:

"Its spray pours out al-ma'un, pouring"

And al-Sabir: the clouds.

(p-243) Sūrat al-Mā'ūn

It is also called Sūrat Ara'ayta (Surah "Have You Seen").

On it there are two views.

The first: it is Meccan. This is the view of the majority.

The second: it is Madinan. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah. Hibat Allah al-Mufassir said: half of it was revealed in Makkah concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il, and half of it in al-Madinah concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy the hypocrite.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Din (Judgment/Religion)?﴾ The scholars differed concerning whom this verse was revealed, into six views.

The first: it was revealed concerning a man among the hypocrites. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: it was revealed concerning 'Amr ibn 'A'idh. This is the view of al-Dahhak.

(p-244) The third: concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. This is the view of al-Suddi.

The fourth: concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il. This is the view of Ibn al-Sa'ib.

The fifth: concerning Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. This is the view of Ibn Juraij.

The sixth: concerning Abu Jahl. This is related by al-Mawardi.

As for "al-Din," there are four views.

The first: that it is the judgment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: the reckoning. This is the view of Mujahid and 'Ikrimah.

The third: the recompense. This is related by al-Mawardi.

The fourth: the Qur'an. This is related by some exegetes. And "yadu'u" means "yadfa'u" (pushes away). We have mentioned it in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The day they will be pushed toward the Fire of Hell with a violent push﴾ [al-Tur: 13]. The meaning is that he pushes the orphan away from his right with a harsh shove, in order to take his wealth. We have already explained earlier that they did not give inheritance to minors. It is said: he pushes the orphan away, driving him off, because he does not hope for reward for feeding him. ﴿And does not urge the feeding of the needy﴾, i.e., he does not feed him, nor does he command that he be fed, because he denies the recompense.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So woe to those who pray﴾ ﴿who are heedless of their prayer﴾. This was revealed concerning the hypocrites who do not hope for reward for their prayer, nor fear punishment for abandoning it. If they are with the Prophet ﷺ, they pray out of showing off; and if they are not with him, they do not pray. This is His saying: ﴿who make show (of their deeds)﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: By Allah, they did not abandon it entirely; and had they abandoned it entirely, they would have been unbelievers, but they neglected guarding its times. Ibn 'Abbas said: they delay it from its time. It is related from Abu al-'Aliyah that he said: it is the one who does not know how many rak'ahs he has prayed, whether an even or an odd number. Some scholars rejected this, saying: this is nothing, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself forgot in his prayer, and because He said ﴿from their prayer﴾ and did not say ﴿in their prayer﴾, and because that hardly falls within the capacity of the son of Adam.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: I say: I do not think Abu al-'Aliyah meant occasional forgetfulness; rather he meant constant forgetfulness, and that indicates the heart's turning away from reverence for the prayer, so the blame falls upon that, not upon forgetfulness.

On "al-Ma'un" there are six views.

The first: that it is the needle, the water, the fire, the axe, and whatever is in the house of this sort. This was related by Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet ﷺ, and Ibn Mas'ud, and Ibn 'Abbas in one report, held a similar view. Abu Salih related from him that he said: al-Ma'un is all good (al-ma'ruf), even mentioning the cooking pot, the bowl, and the axe. 'Ikrimah said: the woe is not for the one who withholds these things; rather the woe is for the one who gathers them, so he shows off in his prayer, forgets it, and withholds these. Al-Zajjaj said: al-Ma'un in the Jahiliyyah was everything that had benefit in it, like the axe, the pot, the bucket, the tinderbox, and the like, and also in Islam.

The second: that it is zakah. This was said by 'Ali, Ibn Ya'mar, al-Hasan, 'Ikrimah, and Qatadah.

The third: that it is obedience. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas in one report.

The fourth: wealth. This was said by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Zuhri.

The fifth: good (al-ma'ruf). This was said by Muhammad ibn Ka'b.

The sixth: water. Al-Farra' mentioned it from some Arabs, saying: and he recited to me:

"Its spray pours out al-ma'un, pouring"

And al-Sabir: the clouds.
